paper.title: Managing Self-Learning Experts under Per-Round Budget Constraints

settings.name_in_paper: Decision making with trainable (self-learning) experts under per-round learning budget M
unmapped: Limited-advice feedback: each round the learner chooses up to M experts to train and observes their realized losses (deployed expert is among them); more informative than pure bandit feedback
Experts are themselves learning algorithms whose loss improves only when they are trained (self-learning / endogenous loss process)
Learner knows each expert's anytime high-probability regret envelope U_k(n, delta) = O(n^alpha c(delta)) (Assumption 2)
Smoothing wrapper assumption (Assumption 3) for constructing deployed decision
settings.definition_quote: At each round $t$, $\mathcal{P}$ allocates the training budget to a subset $S_t \subseteq [K]$ (where $|S_t| \le M$) and selects a global decision $u^t \in \mathbf{U}$ by adopting the advice of a chosen expert. ... The goal of $\mathcal{P}$ is to minimize the cumulative regret relative to the best expert in the pool: $\mathrm{Reg}(T) := \sum_{t=1}^T \ell(u^t, \xi^t) - T \cdot L^\star.$

settings.name_in_paper: Decision making with trainable experts under per-round budget M (lower bound)
unmapped: Limited-advice feedback with per-round training budget M; experts are learning algorithms solving two-armed (or finite-armed) bandit subproblems from a class F_alpha
For alpha > 1/2 losses are non-negative heavy-tailed with bounded (1+beta)-moment (u=1); for alpha <= 1/2 Bernoulli construction possible; alpha=1 uses [0,1] losses with T+1 arms
settings.definition_quote: Consider the single-deployment setting of Section~\ref{sec:losses} with $K$ experts, horizon $T$, and a per-round budget $M$. Fix $\alpha\in[0,1]$. There exists a class $\mathcal F_\alpha$ satisfying Def.~\ref{def:alpha-class}...

symbols.M: per-round training budget (number of experts updated per round), M <= K
symbols.alpha_exp: exponent of the experts' regret envelope U_k(n,delta)=O(n^alpha c(delta))
symbols.c_delta: problem-dependent confidence scaling c(delta), polylog in 1/delta

conditions: each expert satisfies Assumption 2 with U_k(t,delta)=O(t^alpha c(delta)), alpha in (0,1)
tuning: confidence bounds of Definition 1 with delta_arm = delta/(2K), delta_n = delta/(3.5 K n^2)

source.label: thm:gen-rate
source.quote: Let $\alpha, \delta \in (0, 1)$ and each expert $k$ satisfy Asm.~\ref{assumption:expert_regret} with $U_k(t,\delta) =O\big(t^{\alpha}c(\delta)\big)$... Then, with probability at least $1 - \delta$ the regret of Alg.~\ref{algorithm:M_LCB} is bounded for all $T\ge1$ as $\mathrm{Reg}(T) = O\left(\sqrt{\frac{K T}{M}\log(\frac{KT}{\delta})} + \Bigl(\tfrac{K}{M}\Bigr)^{1-\alpha} T^{\alpha} c(\delta)\right).$

results.notes: Regret is realized loss minus T L*. Feedback model (limited advice) not exactly expressible. Remark 2 gives a refined version with per-expert constants beta_k: T^alpha c(delta)[beta_{k*} + ((1/M) sum beta_k^{1/(1-alpha)})^{1-alpha}].

conditions: each expert satisfies Assumption 2 with U_k(t,delta)=O(t^alpha c(delta)), alpha in (0,1]

source.quote: Let $\alpha\in(0,1]$, $\delta\in(0,1)$. Let each expert $k$ satisfy Asm.~\ref{assumption:expert_regret} with $U_k(t,\delta)=O\big(t^{\alpha}c(\delta)\big)$. Run Alg.~\ref{algorithm:M_LCB} ... Then, with probability at least $1 - \delta$ the mean regret of selected arms ... is, for all $T\ge 1$, $\mathrm{Reg}_M(T)= O(...)$

results.notes: Top-M mean regret Reg_M(T) = sum_t [(1/M) sum_{k in S_t} L*_k - mean optimal loss of best M experts], against best M-subset; multiple-play extension. Quantity recorded as other.

bound.regime: sqrt(K log K/(M T)) sufficiently small

symbols.alpha_exp: hardness exponent of the expert task class F_alpha, in [0,1]

conditions: each expert solves a problem from a class F_alpha admitting an alpha-regret lower bound (heavy-tailed two-armed bandits for alpha>1/2)
c_1, c_2 depend only on alpha
holds for any expert algorithms and meta-procedure

source.label: thm:mt-alpha
source.quote: There exists a class $\mathcal F_\alpha$ satisfying Def.~\ref{def:alpha-class}, s.t. if each expert $k \in [K]$ solves a problem $f_k \in \mathcal F_\alpha$, then, for sufficiently small $\sqrt{\frac{K\log K}{MT}}$ and for any algorithm $\mathscr{A}_k$ and meta-procedure $\mathcal{P}$ $\sup \mathbb{E}\,\mathrm{Reg}(T) \ge c_1\,\sqrt{\frac{K\,T}{M}} + c_2\,T^\alpha (K/M)^{1-\alpha}$

results.notes: Restated as Theorem 4 in appendix. E Reg(T) is expectation of realized loss minus T L*, equals pseudo-regret type in expectation; recorded as expected_regret per paper. Noise heavy-tailed for alpha>1/2, bounded for alpha<=1/2 and alpha=1.
